verdict.rationale: Square documents a broad first-party API surface. It covers payments, refunds, disputes, payouts, invoices, subscriptions, team management, catalog, inventory, customers, orders, bookings, gift cards, labor and locations. GraphQL, webhooks, and an official MCP server claiming access to "everything the APIs offer" round this out. However, nothing claims or shows parity with the seller UI. Several UI-facing capabilities have no evidenced API equivalent: custom fraud rules and alerts, targeted email marketing, unified sales reporting, and the Square AI assistant. Missing for 10: an explicit UI–API parity statement, evidenced API coverage of fraud-rule configuration, marketing, and reporting, and independent corroboration that no features are UI-only.
